projects.title: File Guardian
projects.subtitle: Inspect, compare and safely copy your folders.
projects.result: A read-only inventory first, then duplicate reports, copy plans and reversible copies. No automatic deletion of your originals.

projects.title: Equipment Manager
projects.subtitle: Turn sample equipment data into a maintained application.
projects.result: A tested calculation package, CSV imports, SQLite persistence, streaming summaries and a local web interface.

projects.title: Log Analyzer
projects.subtitle: Convert synthetic event exports into traceable reports.
projects.result: Normalize time zones, group evidence, fetch paginated fixtures and generate escaped HTML reports. Read-only by design.

releases.title: 01 / Inventory without touching originals
releases.goal: Produce a deterministic list of files that is safe to inspect.
contract: Implement file_guardian.core.inventory(root: Path) -> list[dict]. Each row has exactly path, size, extension. path is POSIX-style and relative to root; size is bytes; extension is the lowercase final suffix including its dot, or an empty string.
Include regular files in nested directories. Do not follow file or directory symlinks. Sort rows by relative path. Empty directories return [].
Raise FileNotFoundError for a missing root, NotADirectoryError for a file root. Do not read file content or modify any file.
An unreadable directory raises PermissionError instead of silently claiming the inventory is complete. The permission case is self-reviewed across operating systems.

learn.title: Model the output first
learn.text: A list of small dictionaries is sufficient. Separate finding files from displaying or exporting the result.

learn.title: Work with paths
learn.text: Use pathlib for traversal and relative paths. A symlink is not an ordinary directory: decide before you recurse.

learn.title: Build a tiny fixture
learn.text: Create two files and a nested directory in a disposable folder. Predict the records, then inspect their actual byte sizes.

prediction.prompt: A UTF-8 file contains only é. What should size report?
prediction.explanation: The contract measures bytes. UTF-8 encodes this character with two bytes.

hints: First return the relative paths of ordinary files from a tiny fixture.
Check whether an entry is a symlink before recursing or collecting it.
stat().st_size gives bytes; relative_to(root).as_posix() gives the required path.
releases.change_request: A teammate adds filenames containing spaces and Unicode. Add a test first, then show the same inventory contract still works.
acceptance: The official behavior cases pass.
I wrote and ran at least one additional test in tests/.
I compared original file hashes before/after and documented the result.

releases.title: 02 / Detect duplicate content
releases.goal: Find duplicate bytes, not just duplicate filenames.
contract: Implement duplicates(root: Path) -> list[list[str]]. Return groups of at least two equal-content regular files.
Each group contains sorted relative paths. Sort the groups lexicographically by their path lists. Ignore symlinks as in inventory.
Use a streaming SHA-256 digest to group candidates. Different names may hold the same bytes; matching names do not establish equal content.
Empty files can be duplicates. Do not delete or change anything. Document that hash equality is used as an integrity comparison, not identity or authorship.

learn.title: Separate name from content
learn.text: A name tells you where a file is stored, not what it contains. Compare content digests.

learn.title: Keep memory bounded
learn.text: Read chunks from a file rather than loading a large file into memory. A generator or a simple read loop both fit.

prediction.prompt: Two files have the same length but different bytes. Are they duplicates?
prediction.explanation: Length is a useful candidate filter, but does not establish equal content.

hints: Reuse safe traversal from release 1.
Accumulate path lists in a dictionary keyed by the content digest.
Keep only groups with at least two paths; explicitly sort both levels.
releases.change_request: Add empty files and renamed copies to your fixture. Explain which group memberships should change.
acceptance: All provided cases pass.
I added a negative test for equal-length different content.
I reviewed that content reading is chunked.

releases.title: 03 / Preview an organization plan
releases.goal: Propose copies into extension folders without making changes.
contract: Implement plan(root: Path, destination: Path) -> list[dict]. Return sorted actions with exactly source, target, sha256.
source is relative to root. target is <extension-without-dot>/<basename>, using lowercase extension or other/ for no suffix. Preserve filename spelling.
Reject an existing target, two sources mapping to the same target, any destination inside root, or a destination resolving through a symlink. Raise ValueError.
Compute the digest of each source. No directories or files may be created by planning. A missing destination outside root is valid.

learn.title: Planning is a separate operation
learn.text: A dry run should share its decision logic with execution but have no write side effects.

learn.title: Conflicts are part of the contract
learn.text: Two directories can contain the same basename. Refuse ambiguous plans rather than silently choosing a winner.

prediction.prompt: Planning into a missing destination should do what?
prediction.explanation: Planning is strictly read-only, including directory creation.

hints: Start by mapping inventory entries to destination-relative paths.
Use a set of planned targets and separately check existing targets.
Resolve root and destination to compare containment; also reject symlink components before using a path.
releases.change_request: Two subfolders now contain notes.txt. Add the collision test before modifying the planner.
acceptance: All provided cases pass.
I tested that plan leaves root and destination unchanged.
I reviewed canonical path and symlink checks.

releases.title: 04 / Apply an explicit copy plan
releases.goal: Execute an approved plan without removing originals.
contract: Implement apply_plan(root, destination, actions) -> dict. Accept only actions from the release 3 contract. Validate every source, target, digest, duplicate target and existing destination before making a change.
Reject absolute paths, .. segments, and symlink components on both sides with ValueError. Refuse source content changed since planning. Never overwrite an existing file.
Copy files; do not move or delete sources. Return {"schema":1,"files":actions}, and write the same object to destination/manifest.json using UTF-8.

On validation failure, do not create output files. If an OS write fails after execution begins, propagate the exception and document that partial copies may remain. This is not a transactional filesystem.

learn.title: Validate before writes
learn.text: Check the complete plan before starting. That catches stale sources and collisions before avoidable partial work.

learn.title: Failure is not success
learn.text: A disk-full or permission error must not be swallowed. Keep the original files untouched so partial work is recoverable.

prediction.prompt: The source changed after the preview. What should execution do?
prediction.explanation: The user approved a particular content snapshot, not an unknown newer one.

hints: Preflight all actions into a validated list before calling any copy operation.
Compare current source hashes with the planned values.
Create outputs exclusively or recheck carefully; document race limitations rather than claiming adversarial filesystem safety.
releases.change_request: Simulate a write failure in your own test. Confirm originals remain intact and the error is visible.
acceptance: Official cases pass.
I wrote a failure-injection test.
I documented partial-copy and concurrent-filesystem limitations.

releases.title: 05 / Recover and maintain
releases.goal: Undo only the unchanged copies created by a recorded plan.
contract: Implement rollback(destination: Path, manifest: dict) -> dict with removed and skipped arrays of sorted target paths.
Validate schema, unique safe relative targets, and reject symlink/path-escape destinations before modifying anything. Raise ValueError on an unsafe manifest.
Remove a copied file only if it exists as a regular non-symlink file and its SHA-256 still matches. Changed or missing files go in skipped. Do not delete source files or directories.
A second rollback returns the same targets in skipped. Add a real-use maintenance note: problem, reproduction, failing test, repair and version/commit.

learn.title: Undo is another specification
learn.text: A changed copied file may now be valuable. Do not assume yesterday’s manifest is permission to delete today’s data.

learn.title: Maintenance closes the loop
learn.text: Use a disposable fixture first. After the read-only tool is useful, record an actual defect or usability change and add a regression test.

prediction.prompt: A copied file was edited after copying. Rollback should?
choices: Skip it and report that decision
prediction.explanation: Rollback is conditional on unchanged copied content.

hints: Treat the manifest as untrusted input, even if your tool wrote it.
Validate the entire manifest before deleting any matching copies.
Compare the digest again at recovery time and make repeat behavior explicit.
releases.change_request: Rebuild this idea in the log analyzer: repeated imports must not erase or duplicate earlier evidence.
acceptance: Official cases pass.
I have a maintenance note with a regression test.
I can explain which files the recovery procedure is never authorized to delete.

releases.title: 01 / A reusable calculation core
releases.goal: Create validated equipment records and reusable calculations.
contract: Implement validate(records) -> list[dict]. Records contain exactly id (nonempty trimmed string), quantity (nonnegative integer, not bool), and watts (finite nonnegative int/float, not bool). Extra fields may be ignored; duplicate normalized IDs are invalid.
Return new normalized dictionaries. Do not mutate the input. Invalid records raise ValueError.
Implement total_power(records) -> float using validated records. Empty input returns 0.0; reject a nonfinite total.
Keep print/input out of these functions.

learn.title: Choose boundaries
learn.text: Parsing and printing belong outside calculation functions. That makes the same core reusable in a CLI and Flask.

learn.title: A bool is not a device count
learn.text: Python booleans are integer-like, so explicit validation is necessary when the contract excludes them.

prediction.prompt: quantity=True should be accepted as one device?
prediction.explanation: The application contract explicitly excludes booleans.

hints: Validate each field before arithmetic.
Return fresh dictionaries so the caller keeps ownership of its input.
Check math.isfinite both on inputs and the final total.
releases.change_request: Add an item containing a leading/trailing space in its ID. Explain how normalization affects duplicate detection.
acceptance: Behavior cases pass.
My own test checks input immutability.
I can call the core without using a terminal.

releases.title: 02 / CSV import with error records
releases.goal: Preserve good rows while reporting bad ones.
contract: Implement load_csv(path) -> dict with records and errors arrays. Header must include id, quantity, watts; otherwise raise ValueError.

Convert quantity from integer text and watts from float text. Validate each row using release 1. Errors contain exactly line (physical data row number for simple one-line records, starting at 2) and reason (nonempty text).
Keep valid rows in input order; reject duplicate IDs after their first valid occurrence. Empty-with-header is valid.
Never modify the input. Missing files propagate FileNotFoundError. Quoted multiline CSV row line reporting is a documented optional extension.

learn.title: Parsing is not validation
learn.text: CSV fields are text. Convert them, then enforce application rules.

learn.title: Partial import must be honest
learn.text: A useful result reports accepted records and rejected rows separately. Never quietly omit bad rows.

prediction.prompt: A row has watts=nan. float() parses it. Is it valid?
prediction.explanation: Parsing succeeded, but the equipment contract rejects nonfinite values.

hints: Use csv.DictReader rather than splitting every line on commas.
Record an error at the row boundary; do not catch missing-file errors as row errors.
Keep a set of accepted IDs for duplicate checks.
releases.change_request: The supplier adds an extra column. Keep required fields working, then add a test for a missing required header.
acceptance: Cases pass.
My report lists rejected line numbers.
The original CSV is byte-for-byte unchanged.

releases.title: 03 / SQLite persistence and rollback
releases.goal: Store equipment with atomic batch replacement.
contract: Implement save_records(db: Path, records) -> None. Create equipment(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, quantity INTEGER NOT NULL, watts REAL NOT NULL) as needed, then replace the complete inventory in one transaction.
Validate the entire batch before committing. An invalid replacement must leave the previous inventory intact.
Implement list_records(db) -> list[dict], sorted by id, and search(db, identifier) -> dict | None.
Use bound SQL parameters. Names containing apostrophes or SQL-looking text are literal identifiers, not executable SQL.

learn.title: Transactions preserve a coherent state
learn.text: A replacement either commits as a complete valid batch or leaves the previous data intact.

learn.title: Data is not SQL
learn.text: Pass values through placeholders instead of concatenating them into statements.

prediction.prompt: A bad row appears in a replacement batch. The database should contain?
choices: Only the earlier good rows from that batch

hints: Validate before replacing existing records.
Use a connection transaction and parameterized statements.
Test the failed update by reopening the database, not only inspecting in-memory values.
releases.change_request: Add a category in a separate migration exercise; record before/after counts and rollback steps.
acceptance: Cases pass.
My own test proves failed replacement preserves data.
I reviewed SQL parameter binding.

releases.title: 04 / Stream larger inputs
releases.goal: Summarize a one-pass input without materializing it.
contract: Implement summarize_stream(values) -> dict with count, minimum, maximum, mean.
Accept a one-pass iterable of finite numbers, excluding booleans. Empty input returns count=0 and None for the other fields.
Do not iterate twice or convert the input to a list. Invalid data raises ValueError; reject nonfinite intermediate results.
Include your own generator test and explain memory usage independently of file size.

learn.title: Iteration is a protocol
learn.text: An iterable may not support length, indexing or a second pass. Consume it once.

learn.title: Keep only needed state
learn.text: Count, total and extrema are enough for this contract. A generator exposes accidental second passes.

prediction.prompt: You call list(values), then loop values again on a generator. What happens?
prediction.explanation: Most generator objects are consumed by the first iteration.

hints: Start count at zero and extrema unset.
Update count, extrema and total during the same pass.
Do not call len or min/max on the original iterator after consuming it.
releases.change_request: Rebuild in Log Analyzer using a stream of events. Do not copy equipment-specific parsing.
acceptance: Cases pass.
My generator test fails if a second iteration is attempted.

releases.title: 05 / Local Flask interface
releases.goal: Reuse the core behind an HTTP interface.
contract: Create create_app(database_path) in kit_manager/web.py. GET /api/equipment lists sorted records; POST /api/equipment accepts a JSON list and atomically replaces the sample inventory.
Return 400 JSON errors for invalid input, 404 for unknown routes, and a readable UI that distinguishes pending, success and error states.
Use Flask’s test client and your own pytest tests for route behavior. Keep server validation and parameterized SQL. Do not start a server on import.

Run only on localhost with fictional records. Document authentication/CSRF/deployment work required before any public exposure. This release is artifact-reviewed, not automatically certified by the runner.

learn.title: Share the core
learn.text: The web layer translates HTTP to existing functions; it should not duplicate calculations.

learn.title: Test requests without a public server
learn.text: The test client exercises routes locally. Frontend validation never replaces the server contract.

prediction.prompt: A browser validates quantity. The Flask route can skip validation?
prediction.explanation: Requests can bypass the browser form.

hints: Use an application factory with the sample database path passed in.
Call the validated core and persistence functions from routes.
Use textContent or template escaping when displaying user labels.
releases.change_request: Write a test for an invalid replacement submitted over HTTP and prove the earlier valid inventory survives.
acceptance: I recorded a repository commit and how to run it.
Route tests cover valid, invalid and missing routes.
Keyboard and narrow-screen checks are recorded.
Production/security limitations are documented.

releases.title: 06 / Package, release and maintain
releases.goal: Let another person install and reproduce the result.
contract: Add a documented CLI entry point with --help, list, import and report operations. Use meaningful nonzero exit codes for failures.
Build an installable distribution from pyproject.toml. In a clean virtual environment, install it and run your tests and CLI without relying on the source working directory.
Create a versioned commit and record exact commands, Python/dependency versions and observed outputs.
After using it, document a real change, add a failing regression test, repair it and create a new version. This is reviewed evidence, not an automatic release badge.

learn.title: A release is reproducible
learn.text: A working checkout is not necessarily an installable package. Test outside the project directory.

learn.title: Use a version trail
learn.text: Record the revision associated with every test run. A changed requirement creates a new evidence record.

prediction.prompt: Tests work only when run inside src/. Is that enough for a release?
prediction.explanation: Installation and execution should not depend on an accidental working directory.

hints: Use the included pyproject.toml as the packaging scaffold.
Install the distribution in a new environment and run --help from another directory.
Keep sample data and run instructions independent of your personal paths.
releases.change_request: Ask someone to follow the README on a clean environment and turn their first failure into a regression test.
acceptance: A clean-install transcript is attached.
CLI help and failure exit codes are tested.
Repository revision and dependency versions are recorded.
A later maintenance change has a reproducible regression test.

releases.title: 01 / Normalize event timestamps
releases.goal: Convert synthetic exports into stable UTC records.
contract: Implement normalize(events) -> dict with records and errors. Input events have id, account, at, and optional ip. IDs/accounts must be nonempty strings.
Parse ISO-8601 at values with an explicit offset or Z. Reject naive timestamps. Emit UTC ISO strings with seconds and +00:00. Retain exactly id, account, at, ip (None if absent).
First valid occurrence of an event ID wins; ignore later duplicates. Invalid records produce errors with index (zero-based) and nonempty reason.
Sort valid records by UTC timestamp then id. Inputs must remain unchanged. Do not infer a person’s identity from an IP.

learn.title: Store a comparable time
learn.text: Offsets matter: different wall-clock strings can name the same instant.

learn.title: Separate observations from identity
learn.text: Normalize the evidence. Do not invent location or compromise claims from missing data.

prediction.explanation: UTC is four hours ahead of that offset.

hints: Require timezone-aware datetimes before converting to UTC.
Reject incomplete records at the record boundary and retain their input indexes.
Deduplicate valid event IDs, then sort normalized records.
releases.change_request: Add two equivalent instants with different offsets and an event arriving out of order. Predict the final order first.
acceptance: Cases pass.
My own offset-boundary test is recorded.
No missing information is invented.

releases.title: 02 / Traceable account summaries
releases.goal: Every count must be traceable to supporting event IDs.
contract: Implement summarize(events) -> list[dict], using normalized valid and deduplicated records.
Return account, count, ips and event_ids for each account. ips contains sorted distinct nonempty strings; event_ids follows normalized chronological order. Sort rows by account.
Ignore invalid inputs in the summary but preserve their diagnostics through normalize().
Do not label events malicious. These are descriptive observations.

learn.title: Make aggregates inspectable
learn.text: Keep the supporting identifiers next to a count so a report can be audited.

learn.title: Do not count duplicates twice
learn.text: Normalization and deduplication should happen before grouping.

prediction.prompt: The same event arrives twice. Its account count increases by?
prediction.explanation: The same unique event ID contributes one observation.

hints: Call the normalization function instead of repeating date parsing.
Group by account and keep both a count and supporting IDs.
Use a set for distinct IP strings, then sort for deterministic output.
releases.change_request: Write a test showing that adding a duplicate does not alter the report. Compare this with File Guardian duplicate semantics.
acceptance: Cases pass.
Each total has supporting event IDs.
I added an idempotence test.

releases.title: 03 / Robust pagination adapter
releases.goal: Handle API-shaped pages without requiring live credentials.
contract: Implement fetch_all(fetch_page, max_pages=100, retries=2) -> list. fetch_page(cursor) is an injected callable; first cursor is None.
Each response is {"items":list, "next": string-or-None}. Preserve page/item order. None means finished.
Retry TimeoutError up to retries extra calls per page, then propagate it. Do not return a partial result as success. Reject malformed responses and repeated cursors with ValueError.
Raise ValueError if max_pages is reached while another page remains. Tests use a fake fetcher, no network. Later bind a read-only HTTPS client with explicit timeout and credentials outside source.

learn.title: Separate transport from logic
learn.text: An injected function makes failure behavior reproducible without a network or credentials.

learn.title: Bound your retries
learn.text: Retries need a limit. A repeating cursor must not create an infinite loop.

prediction.prompt: retries=2 allows how many attempts per page including the first?
prediction.explanation: Two retries are in addition to the initial call.

hints: Test two successful pages before adding retries.
Remember cursors already visited. Validate the response shape each time.
Only return after a terminal page; propagate exhausted failures.
releases.change_request: Connect a fake provider returning an error after one good page. Confirm no partial-success report is emitted.
acceptance: Cases pass.
Timeout and repeating-cursor tests are recorded.
A real client would have explicit timeout and a restricted read-only credential.

releases.title: 04 / Escaped HTML report
releases.goal: Build a portable report with traceable observations.
contract: Implement render_html(events) -> str. Produce a complete UTF-8 HTML document with a title and a table with Account, Count, IPs, Event IDs headings.
Use normalized account summaries. Escape all untrusted account/IP/event-id text. No script elements, external resources, inline handlers, or active network calls.
Render one table row per account in sorted order. Display supporting IDs and an explicit empty-state message when no valid records exist.
Add a maintenance note with the first defect you found and the test that catches it. Report remains read-only.

learn.title: Report data is still untrusted
learn.text: Logs can contain attacker-controlled strings. HTML escaping applies even to an offline report.

learn.title: A useful artifact travels
learn.text: A self-contained document can be opened without your Python environment. Keep it free of external requests.

prediction.prompt: An account is named <script>alert(1)</script>. Display it how?
prediction.explanation: Preserve the observation while preventing execution.

hints: Use html.escape for every value placed into HTML text.
Generate summaries first, then render them.
Test the document with html.parser, not only by looking at a screenshot.
releases.change_request: Import events with HTML-looking labels and Unicode names. Keep the evidence readable and inert.
acceptance: Official cases pass.
My own regression test checks escaped labels.
The empty-state and supporting IDs are visible.
